questions.question: A slack adjuster should move no more than ____ from where it is attached to the push rod.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check each slack adjuster. Park the truck, set wheel chocks, and disengage the parking brake. Pull the slack adjusters. They should not move more than one inch from where the push rod is attached. If they move more than one inch, they are out of adjustment and need to be fixed.

questions.question: Be sure that your wheel bearing and seals are:
questions.explanation: During an inspection, check that the wheel bearing and seals are not leaking.

questions.question: To prevent trailers from rolling over, a driver should do all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: To reduce the risk of a rollover, drive slowly when turning and on curves. Steer gently and smoothly. When loading trailers, keep the cargo as low to the ground as possible.

questions.question: After a tire has been changed, the driver should stop after a short distance to:

options.text: Recheck the tightness of the lug nuts.
See if rocks have gotten into the tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Recheck the tightness of the lug nuts.
questions.explanation: After you start driving with a new tire, stop after a short distance. Recheck that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: Driving at night is usually:

options.text: More difficult than driving during the day.
Simpler than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more difficult than day driving for several reasons. It is harder to see hazards. Headlight glare can affect your vision. There are more tired drivers on the road.

questions.question: When a tire goes flat, you may hear a loud bang. The truck will be affected:

options.text: Only if the damaged tire is near the front of the truck.
Only if the truck is hauling a load.

questions.explanation: There may be a delay of a few seconds between when you hear the tire fail and when the truck is affected. Because of this delay, you might think the sound came from another vehicle.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that you could slow down other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Drive with your emergency flashers activated.
Wave an arm out of your window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with your emergency flashers activated.
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly, use your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Check that local laws allow this.

questions.question: If planning to stop on the road to unload cargo, you should:

options.text: Stop suddenly, since you are already on the road.
Warn other drivers by tapping your brakes.
Wave your arm out the window to get the attention of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers by tapping your brakes.
questions.explanation: Tap your brakes and flash your brake lights to warn other drivers any time you plan to slow or stop unexpectedly. Use this method when stopping on the road to unload cargo or passengers.

questions.question: When you are driving while drowsy, you should:

options.text: Press on and try to finish the trip.

questions.explanation: The only effective way to deal with drowsiness while driving is to stop and sleep. Caffeine and other drugs may help you stay awake, but they will not keep you alert. You will feel even more tired when the effects wear off.

questions.question: A burning tire should be:
questions.explanation: Cool a burning tire with water. You may need to use large amounts of water to cool it properly.

questions.question: You should slow down and be extra careful:
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful when driving near work zones. Also be careful where pavement drops off at the road edge, when objects are on the road, and on freeway ramps.

questions.question: A distracted driver:

options.text: Usually follows the rules of the road.
Is a good driver to follow.

questions.explanation: Distracted drivers notice dangers on the road later than focused drivers. They may not notice hazards at all.

questions.question: A lightly-loaded combination vehicle stops more slowly than a fully-loaded vehicle because:

options.text: The stiff suspension springs and strong brakes will have high traction.
The stiff suspension springs and strong brakes will have low traction.
The brakes only work when a trailer reaches a minimum weight.
The suspension springs only work when a trailer reaches a minimum weight.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stiff suspension springs and strong brakes will have low traction.
questions.explanation: An empty combination vehicle stops more slowly than a fully-loaded one. The stiff suspension springs and strong brakes have less grip on a light trailer than on a heavier vehicle.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, you should:
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not brake. Instead, release the accelerator and push in the clutch. This helps you regain traction.

questions.question: If a trailer starts to skid, the driver should:
questions.explanation: If your trailer skids while braking, release the brakes. This lets the wheels grip the road again. Once traction returns, the trailer will straighten out and follow the tractor.

questions.question: In an emergency situation, you should:

options.text: Always turn on your flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the safest choice during an emergency. It is usually safer to steer around the hazard to avoid a crash.

questions.question: When traveling down a hill:

options.text: You will slow to a stop.

questions.explanation: When driving downhill, gravity pulls your vehicle faster. Your speed increases.

questions.question: When driving, keeping space between your vehicle and other vehicles is:
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your vehicle and others is essential for safety. It gives you room to stop if needed without hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: If a vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, the driver should:

options.text: Stay in the vehicle and try to restart it.
Get out of the vehicle and walk away from the tracks.
Try to flag down another vehicle for a push.
Wait in the vehicle for a police officer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave the vehicle immediately and move away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information on signs at the crossing. Call that number or call 911.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS):

options.text: Are only used on trucks carrying hazardous materials.
Help drivers stay in control when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help drivers stay in control when braking.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheels from locking up when the brakes are applied hard.
